subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the remaining gap, but the change would add public config and alter user-visible failed-mutation warning semantics that automation should not choose on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove unresolved failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or specific remaining channel leaks.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle channel-specific or tool-class-specific leaks in narrower issues before designing a shared policy.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove unresolved failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the warning-policy function and authored the merged PR that explicitly left this broader issue open.
